records.name_note: Naming is split across the dedicated single-species pages, and the disputed names overlap with a sibling species already in this catalog. NC State's Common Name(s) field carries seven entries in alphabetical order -- American Hop-hornbeam, Eastern Hop Hornbeam, Hop Hornbeam, Hop Horn Beam, Ironwood, Leverwood, Wooly Hop hornbeam -- and its first entry, American Hop-hornbeam, is also the first name in the page title's parenthetical; NC State's Description prose, however, opens 'Eastern hop-hornbeam, is a slender deciduous tree in the Betulaceae (birch) family.' MoBot's displayed field reads 'Common Name: eastern hop hornbeam,' but MoBot's own Noteworthy Characteristics prose opens 'Ostrya virginiana, commonly called American hop hornbeam, is a deciduous, Missouri native tree...' and later adds 'Also commonly called ironwood because of its extremely hard and dense wood.' RHS's plant profile shows the binomial as its H1 with 'American hop hornbeam' as the rendered subtitle, and lists 'American hop hornbeam, Eastern hop hornbeam, ironwood, leverwood' under Other common names. UF/IFAS's fact sheet is titled 'Ostrya virginiana: American Hophornbeam' and its Common name(s) field reads 'American Hophornbeam, Eastern Hophornbeam,' whose first entry matches the title. The American-prefixed name therefore leads on NC State (title parenthetical and first Common Name(s) entry), RHS (subtitle and first Other common names entry), UF/IFAS (title and first field entry) and MoBot's prose, while the Eastern-prefixed name leads MoBot's structured Common Name field and NC State's Description sentence; this record uses the American-led name. 'Ironwood' is not used as the lead: NC State's 'is often confused with' module for Ostrya virginiana names Carpinus caroliniana, and NC State's page title for Carpinus caroliniana carries Ironwood in its own parenthetical common-name list, so this catalog treats Ironwood as a collision name shared with a species already catalogued as b63 -- the inference is the catalog's, not NC State's. 'Leverwood' appears only as a secondary entry (NC State's list, RHS's Other common names) and never leads a title, subtitle or prose sentence on any admissible page, so it is not used either. Clemson HGIC's 'Plants for Damp or Wet Areas' factsheet lists 'Ostrya virginiana – Hop Hornbeam,' but that is an entry in a multi-species factsheet rather than a dedicated species page, so it is not counted toward the name tally.
unknowns: No admissible source addresses toxicity to cats or dogs specifically for Ostrya virginiana; NC State's page carries no Poison Part or Poisonous plant-type/problem tag at all, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null rather than inferred.

chill_damage_f and cool_rest_note left null: NC State gives a USDA Plant Hardiness Zone range (3a-9b) and UF/IFAS gives USDA zones 3A-9A, but both are survival/hardiness-zone ratings, not a stated damage-onset temperature, so per the rules they cannot be used to fill chill_damage_f.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, light_fc_good and direct_sun_hours_max are all left null: no admissible source gives species-specific numeric temperature, humidity, footcandle, or direct-sun-hour prose for this tree (NC State's Light field only carries its site-wide generic hour-range legend text, which the rules say may not be used for direct_sun_hours_max).

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State's Soil pH field lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0), AND Alkaline (>8.0) -- since both open-ended bands (Acid and Alkaline) are present alongside Neutral, no ceiling or floor can be responsibly read off the closed Neutral band. UF/IFAS's Soil tolerances field independently corroborates tolerance at both ends ('alkaline; acidic'), so no numeric pH bound is set.

water_regime, water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis all left null: no admissible source frames watering as a regime/schedule for this in-ground tree. MoBot's structured Water field reads 'Water: Medium,' which per the rules is mid-scale and cannot itself support keep_moist or any other regime value; it is noted here only as a disclosed, non-adopted data point.

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength left null: no admissible source gives a fertilizer schedule or dilution strength for this species; UF/IFAS's pest-management prose mentions 'regular fertilization' only as a borer/canker-stress-reduction aside, not a schedule, and per the rules a genus/commercial-production framing would not qualify even if present.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes part_sun: UF/IFAS's Light requirement field lists 'partial sun' as well as 'full sun, ... partial shade, shade tolerant,' but neither of the two North American structured sun fields used as primary (NC State's Light field: Deep shade, Full sun, Partial Shade; MoBot's Sun field: Full sun to part shade) carries a partial-sun value, so per the rules that UF/IFAS-only value is disclosed rather than carried into the list.

RHS's plant-profile page for Ostrya virginiana (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/12014/ostrya-virginiana/details) rendered inconsistently during this research session: an unauthenticated fetch/scroll on this URL at one point swapped in content for a different species (Celtis occidentalis), matching the exact caching hazard this task warned about. Only the H1 ('Ostrya virginiana'), subtitle ('American hop hornbeam') and Other common names line were captured on freshly-verified, title-matched loads and are cited here; RHS's Position, Soil, pH and Name Status fields could not be reliably re-confirmed on a matching page within this session and so are not cited or used for any field.

Clemson HGIC's 'Plants for Damp or Wet Areas' factsheet lists Ostrya virginiana ('Hop Hornbeam') among many species suited to damp/wet siting. Per the rules this is a section inside a multi-species publication, not a dedicated species care page, so it was not used to support soil_drainage, water_regime, or any other field, despite it sitting in some tension with UF/IFAS's and NC State's descriptions of the species tolerating dry, well-drained sites and disliking wet soil.

fieldreport.caes.uga.edu, extension.psu.edu, extension.umd.edu, and hgic.clemson.edu were checked but yielded no dedicated Ostrya virginiana species page (only passing mentions in unrelated or multi-species pages), so none of those domains contributed citations beyond the Clemson wet-areas list noted above.

records.name_note: Sources split on the lead common name. NC State's Common Name(s) field lists nine stacked entries -- American Basswood, American Linden, Basswood, Bee Tree, Carolina Basswood, Lime Tree, Linden, White Basswood, White Wood -- in alphabetical order matching the page-title parenthetical, so its first entry does not mark a preferred name; NC State's Description opens 'American linden is a useful large shade tree in the Malvaceae (mallow) family that is found in all areas of North Carolina.' MoBot renders 'Common Name: American linden' (a longer list sits behind a popup whose text exists only in the link's markup, so it is not quoted), and its Noteworthy Characteristics opens 'Tilia americana, commonly called American basswood or American linden...'. RHS's subtitle is 'American lime' and its Other common names field reads 'American basswood, American linden, American whitewood, basswood, whitewood'. Only one dedicated page -- MoBot's -- actually leads with American linden, in its single-value Common Name field; NC State's body prose (not its title or its name list) also opens with that name, which is why it was preferred over RHS's American lime. The auditor also found species-specific Penn State and University of Maryland pages ('A Native Tree for You to Love: The American Linden'; 'Native Trees of Maryland - The Tree That Sings: American Basswood (Tilia americana)'), one leading with each name; no URL for either is in this record, so they are noted, not cited. Bare 'Linden' and 'Basswood' are genus-level names and not used as the lead.

records.name_note: Sources split on which form of the common name leads. NC State's Common Name(s) list carries eleven stacked entries -- Beaver Tree, Castorwood, Small Laurel Magnolia, Small Magnolia, Swamp Magnolia, Sweetbay, Sweet Bay, Sweet Bay Magnolia, Sweetbay Magnolia, Sweet Magnolia, White Laurel -- alphabetized, so its first entry does not mark a primary name; the page's body prose leads with the two-word 'sweet bay magnolia.' MoBot's displayed Common Name field independently gives the same two-word 'sweet bay magnolia' (its longer Common Names list sits behind a popup whose text exists only as entity-encoded markup in the link's overlib attribute, so it is not quoted here). RHS's subtitle gives simply 'sweet bay,' and its Other common names list -- beaver tree, beaverwood, castorwood, elk bark, small laurel magnolia, swamp bay, swamp laurel, swamp sassafras, white bay, white laurel -- does not include 'swamp magnolia.' UF/IFAS's fact sheet is titled 'Magnolia virginiana: Sweetbay Magnolia' and its Common name(s) line reads 'sweetbay magnolia, swamp magnolia,' leading with the one-word form. We use 'Sweetbay Magnolia' as the catalog-facing name, matching UF/IFAS's title and lead entry and one of NC State's own listed entries; 'Swamp Magnolia' and 'Sweet Bay Magnolia' are recorded here as synonyms rather than the lead.
unknowns: No admissible source (NC State, MoBot, Clemson, UF/IFAS, RHS) carries any toxicity/poison information for this species, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null.

Soil pH: NC State's field is the open-ended 'Acid (<6.0)' band (no closed neutral band to derive a ceiling from), and RHS's categorical pH field is 'Acid or Neutral' with no numeric range and no alkaline listed, so no numeric soil_ph_min/max could be derived; the species is acid-soil-preferring per every admissible source that addresses it.
water_regime is set to keep_moist on the same NC State cultivation prose; MoBot's structured 'Water: Medium to wet' field is a disclosed mid-scale counterpoint.

No admissible source gives numeric footcandle light levels, a species-specific direct-sun-hours limit, day/night temperature ranges, a chill-damage onset temperature, humidity needs, or a fertilizer schedule/strength for this species, so those fields are left null.
water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, and the day-interval watering fields are left null because no source frames watering for this in-ground landscape tree in those terms.

This is a distinct species record from the catalog's existing Magnolias (M. grandiflora, M. stellata, M. x soulangeana, at b24/b34/b42); every value above was drawn from Magnolia virginiana-specific pages/sections, not a cultivar or the genus-umbrella term.

soil_drainage is moderate: NC State's structured Soil Drainage field (Good Drainage, Moist, Occasionally Wet), RHS's Moisture field (Moist but well-drained or Well-drained), RHS's and Clemson's cultivation prose and UF/IFAS's 'wet to well-drained' all read at the moderate end; NC State's 'does best in consistently moist to wet' and its and MoBot's 'tolerates wet, swampy, and boggy soils' are disclosed as the wet-tolerance counterpoint -- this species tolerates wet ground that most magnolias do not, but no source requires it.

2026-09-03 landing: soil_drainage changed from moisture_retentive to moderate on the auditor's finding -- the wet reading rested on tolerance clauses while NC State's own structured Soil Drainage field (never cited by the record) and every other source read moderate; the structured fields are now the primary citations and the wet sentences are disclosed. name_note replaced with the auditor's corrected wording (no invented convention; the invented RHS rationale about 'magnolia' dropped; RHS's subtitle and Other common names now cited).

records.name_note: Three sources with dedicated pages for this species lead with 'Carolina silverbell.' NC State's Common Name(s) field lists six entries alphabetically (Carolina Silverbell, Common Silverbell, Little Silverbell, Mountain Silverbell, Silver Bell, Snowbell Tree); its first entry matches the first name in the page-title parenthetical, and NC State's description text uses only 'Carolina silverbell.' MoBot's Common Name field reads 'Carolina silverbell' (a longer list sits behind a popup whose text exists only in the link's markup, so it is not quoted), and its prose opens 'Halesia carolina, commonly called Carolina silverbell or silverbell tree'. RHS's document title reads 'Halesia carolina | Carolina silverbell,' with opossum wood, silverbell tree and snowdrop tree placed under a separate 'Other common names' heading. Clemson's factsheet is headed 'Silverbells' and covers this species together with two-winged silverbell (Halesia diptera), so bare 'Silverbell' there is a two-species heading, not a name for this species; none of the three dedicated pages leads with 'Mountain Silverbell' or with bare 'Silverbell.' On taxonomy, MoBot states it is 'Synonymous with Halesia tetraptera' and Clemson writes 'Carolina silverbell (Halesia tetraptera; formerly H. carolina),' but RHS's Name Status for Halesia carolina reads 'Correct' with Halesia tetraptera's own RHS page marked 'Synonym,' and NC State's Halesia carolina page lists 'Halesia tetraptera' under 'Previously known as' and says the two are treated as synonyms, so scientific_name_accepted is kept as Halesia carolina.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State Plant Toolbox's structured tag list marks this species "#non-toxic for cats," "#non-toxic for dogs," and "#non-toxic for horses." The page carries no Poison block at all (no Poison Severity, Poison Symptoms, Poison Toxic Principle, or Poison Part fields), so beyond the non-toxic tags there is no further symptom, severity, or poison-part detail to report from admissible sources.
unknowns: water_regime left null: the only structured watering field found is MoBot's 'Water: Medium,' which per the schema's rules is mid-scale and does not support keep_moist; no admissible source gives a species-specific watering statement that maps cleanly to one of the four enum values.

soil_ph_max left null: Clemson's genus factsheet gives an explicit acidic range (pH 5.0 to 6.0) for wild silverbell soils, but RHS's pH field for Halesia carolina lists 'Acid or Neutral' as acceptable and NC State's own Soil pH field lists both an open-ended Acid (<6.0) band and a Neutral (6.0-8.0) band as tolerated; since two sources support soils extending above 6.0, no ceiling is set. Only the acidic floor (5.0) from Clemson is retained, and even that is a wild-habitat 'where they naturally occur' statement rather than a direct cultivation directive.

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength all left null: Clemson's genus factsheet recommends fertilizing 'acid-loving trees in the spring' with an azalea & camellia fertilizer or acid-forming organic fertilizer, but gives no literal numeric interval, no specific months, and no dilution/strength fraction, so none of these fields could be populated without guessing beyond what the source states.

is_houseplant, day/night temperature fields, humidity_need/pct, chill_damage_f, cool_rest_note, and light_fc_min/good all left null (except is_houseplant=false) because no admissible source addresses container/indoor cultivation, ambient temperature bands, relative humidity percentages, a numeric chill-damage onset temperature, or footcandle light levels for this species.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: no species-specific prose (as opposed to NC State's generic site-wide light-category legend) states a maximum direct-sun-hour figure for this species.

water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_dry_down_target, and water_estimate_basis all left null: as an in-ground tree, no admissible source frames its watering as a dry-down depth check or a day-interval schedule.

The UF/IFAS EDIS species page for Halesia carolina (ENH447/ST288) returned HTTP 410 Gone on both edis.ifas.ufl.edu and ask.ifas.ufl.edu at the time of research, so no EDIS-specific data could be used for this species despite edis.ifas.ufl.edu being an admissible domain.

No dedicated extension.umd.edu, fieldreport.caes.uga.edu, or extension.psu.edu page for Halesia carolina was found; a Penn State page mentions Carolina silverbell only in passing as juglone-tolerant within a multi-species walnut-companion article, which does not map to any schema field and was not used.
outdoor_sun_exposure omits part_sun and full_shade: neither NC State's Light field, MoBot's Sun field, nor RHS's Position field lists either of those values for this species.

soil_ph_min left null: the only numeric figure is Clemson's two-species wild-habitat range (pH 5.0 to 6.0), and NC State's Soil pH field is the open-ended Acid (<6.0) band plus Neutral (6.0-8.0), which supplies no floor; RHS's pH field reads Acid or Neutral.
